Scenario

Road and bridge infrastructure requires continuous monitoring to identify structural cracks and surface deterioration before severe infrastructure failure occurs.

Traditional manual inspection methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, inconsistent, and difficult to scale across large infrastructure systems.

This project presents an AI-Based Road and Bridge Crack Detection System developed by Paarthipa Harish and Kamlesh using Computer Vision, FastAPI APIs, AI-assisted reasoning workflows, interactive dashboards, and automated reporting systems.

The system enables users to:

  • Upload crack images
  • Perform automated crack detection
  • Extract crack dimensions
  • Analyze crack severity
  • Generate AI-assisted reasoning outputs
  • Create automated inspection-support reports
  • Visualize infrastructure damage analytics

The project combines AI reasoning systems, backend crack analysis pipelines, visualization dashboards, and automated reporting workflows into a unified infrastructure inspection platform.

Step-By-Step Scenario-Based Workflow

Step 1: Capture Infrastructure Images

Road or bridge crack images are collected using cameras, inspection devices, or mobile devices.

Step 2: Upload Crack Image

Users upload crack images through the frontend interface or notebook workflow.

  • Image upload

Step 3: Backend Processing

The uploaded image is sent to the FastAPI backend for crack analysis and feature extraction.

  • Streamlit backend execution
  • Processing workflow
  • Terminal execution logs

Step 4: Crack Detection and Feature Extraction

The backend extracts:

  • Crack length
  • Crack width
  • Severity level
  • Damage location
  • Structural indicators

  • Crack detection result

Step 5: AI Reasoning Engine Processing

The reasoning engine developed by Paarthipa Harish interprets crack severity and generates intelligent inspection insights.

  • AI reasoning response

Step 6: Visualization Dashboard Analysis

Interactive graphs and visual analytics are generated including:

  • Severity gauges
  • Heatmaps
  • Growth prediction graphs
  • Pie charts
  • Radar analysis

  • Graphs
  • Heatmap
  • Severity gauge

Step 7: Automated Report Generation

The reporting workflow developed by Kamlesh generates inspection-support reports containing measurements, severity analysis, and recommendations.

  • Generated report
  • JSON output

Step 8: AI Chatbot Assistance

Users interact with the AI chatbot to ask infrastructure inspection questions.

  • Chatbot interaction

Step 9: Human Inspection Review

Infrastructure engineers review AI-generated outputs and use them for maintenance planning.

fig = px.bar(
    x=["Length", "Width"],
    y=[data["crack_length"], data["crack_width"]],

    text_auto=True,

fig.show()
In [9]:
severity_map = {
    "Low": 1,
    "Medium": 2,
    "High": 3
}

value = severity_map[data["severity"]]

fig = go.Figure(go.Indicator(
    mode="gauge+number",
    value=value,
    title={'text': "Severity"},
    gauge={
        'axis': {'range': [0, 3]},
        'bar': {'color': "#0f9295"}
    }
))

fig.show()
In [10]:
fig = px.pie(
    names=["Crack", "Remaining"],
    values=[data["crack_width"], max(20 - data["crack_width"], 1)],
    hole=0.5,
    color_discrete_sequence=["#14c9cb", "#baeaeb"]
)

fig.show()
In [11]:
time = np.arange(0, 10)

growth = data["crack_width"] * (1 + 0.1 * time)

fig = px.line(
    x=time,
    y=growth,
    title="Crack Growth Prediction",
    labels={
        "x": "Time",
        "y": "Predicted Crack Width"
    }
)

fig.show()
In [12]:
fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Scatterpolar(
    r=[
        data["crack_length"],
        data["crack_width"],
        {"Low":1,"Medium":2,"High":3}[data["severity"]]
    ],
    theta=["Length", "Width", "Severity"],
    fill='toself'
))

fig.show()
